name: F3: a sub-table box change only re-applies the sub-table text
why: Restores the old listener, applySubFilter(), which filters by the sub-table TEXT alone. The box also governs that sub-table's column filters, so a typed '^Tun' stays literal (0 rows) after ticking Rx until the next keystroke. Must fail on the Rx test (expects 1 row with no keystroke after the tick).

name: F3: applySubTableModes() never re-runs runFilter()
why: Keeps the new listener but drops its runFilter() branch, so the helper degrades to the text-only path. Must fail on the Ex test: 'tunnel' stays at 1 row instead of the inverted 5.

edits.find:
if (hasColFilter && typeof runFilter === 'function') runFilter();
            else textOnly();

name: F3: the text-only branch does nothing
why: Removes the cheap branch's call. With no column filter typed, ticking the sub-table Ex must still invert the sub-table TEXT filter (applySubFilter()). This is what makes the 'guard: F3' test a guard: it fails when the branch the fix kept is lost.

name: F4: the h3 status labels the global query with the sub-table's boxes
why: The original applySubFilter() defect in its shared form: the GLOBAL part is labelled with the sub-table's flags instead of the global ones. With the sub-table Cc on and the global Cc off the span reads GLOBAL:(case) "e". Must fail.
grep: F4: the sub-table status labels the global query

name: F4: the global Ex is never reported
why: _globalFilterFlags() always reports Ex off — what applySubFilter() used to print (it never looked at the global Ex). Must fail on the global-Ex test (GLOBAL:(ex) "zzqq" expected).
grep: F4: the sub-table status shows the global Ex

name: F4: the h3 status counts rows the sub-table filter hid
why: Counts every tbody row instead of the shown ones — the shape of runFilter()'s old count, which took the group's rows before the sub-table filter hid any. 'tunnel' leaves 1 of 6 rows shown; the span must say 1. Must fail.
grep: keeps the row count the sub-table filter left

name: F5: the image-row snapshot compiles the global query with the sub-table flags
why: Restores _artHighlightArtCell()'s ctxSnap to the sub-table's Cc/Rx. It runs LAST after every art-cell rebuild and unwraps earlier marks first, so a global regexp with the sub-table Rx off is compiled literally and the 'Back' badge loses its highlight. Must fail on both F5 tests.

name: F5: runFilter() overwrites the highlight context with the sub-table flags again
why: Restores the overwrite of _activeFilterHighlightCtx.isRegExp/isCaseSensitive in runFilter()'s multi-table loop. That context feeds the BUILD-time highlight in _artBuildMultiRowArtCell(); _artHighlightArtCell() then unwraps those marks and re-applies them from its own (correct) snapshot, so nothing on screen changes. KNOWN OVERLAP, recorded rather than hidden: the spec cannot see this half while the other half is in place.

name: F6: the cached row text joins cells with a space again
why: _cachedFullText() goes back to the whole-row walk, so 'Rest Bruce' matches across the Release and Artist cells. Must fail on both cross-cell tests (multi and single).

name: F6: getCleanVisibleText() ignores the separator it is given
why: The per-cell texts are joined with a space instead of cellSeparator — the separator is requested but never lands. Must fail on the cross-cell tests.

name: F6: the separator also splits text nodes inside one cell
why: The over-eager version of the fix: text nodes are joined with U+001F too, not only cells. A name and its disambiguation comment ('CBS/Sony (imprint') are two nodes of ONE cell and must stay matchable. This is what the 'guard: F6' test exists for. Must fail.

why: _resolveColFilterFlags()'s fallback returns all-off. That would change the single-table rule itself (the global Ex governs every column filter), which F3–F7 deliberately leave alone: the Release filter must still invert to 52 rows. Must fail.
